glossary.Fatigue: Extreme tiredness or lack of energy not relieved by rest.
glossary.Malaise: A general feeling of being unwell, tired and uncomfortable.
glossary.Functional impairment: Difficulty carrying out normal roles such as work, study or self-care.
glossary.Viral illness: An infection caused by a virus, such as flu or glandular fever.
glossary.Intermittently: Coming and going rather than continuous.
glossary.Debilitating: Severely weakening, so normal activity becomes very hard.
glossary.NICE: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence: the UK body that publishes clinical guidelines.
glossary.Cognitive: Relating to thinking, memory and concentration.
glossary.Inflammation: The body's response to injury or infection, causing redness, heat, swelling and pain.
glossary.Tender glands: Sore, swollen lymph nodes, usually felt in the neck.
glossary.Hallmark: The most characteristic feature of a condition.
glossary.Social isolation: Losing contact with friends, family and community.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from the history and examination, with no confirmatory test.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: measures haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&E: Urea and electrolytes: a blood test of kidney function and salts.
glossary.LFTs: Liver function tests: bloods showing liver damage or reduced liver function.
glossary.Mimic: A condition that produces similar symptoms and can be mistaken for another.
glossary.Anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
glossary.Diabetes: A condition of high blood glucose due to lack of insulin or resistance to it.
glossary.Inflammatory disease: A condition driven by ongoing inflammation, such as rheumatoid arthritis or lupus.
glossary.Non-specific tenderness: Pain on pressing that does not point to any particular structure or disease.
glossary.Validate: Acknowledge to the patient that their symptoms are real and taken seriously.
glossary.Non-pharmacological: Treatment that does not use medicines.
glossary.Relapse: A return or worsening of symptoms after a period of improvement.
glossary.Overexertion: Doing more activity than the body can cope with.
glossary.Rehabilitation: Treatment to help regain function and independence.
glossary.Musculoskeletal: Relating to muscles, bones and joints.
glossary.Occupational support: Help with returning to or staying in work, such as adjusted hours or duties.
glossary.Dehydration: Too little water in the body.
glossary.Malnutrition: Lacking adequate nutrition from poor intake or absorption.
glossary.Self-care: Looking after one's own basic needs such as washing, dressing and eating.
glossary.Pathophysiology: The abnormal processes in the body that cause a disease.
glossary.Energy metabolism: How cells convert food into usable energy, mainly in mitochondria.
glossary.Infective trigger: An infection that sets off a longer-lasting illness.
glossary.Exercise tolerance: How much physical activity a person can do before symptoms stop them.
glossary.Side effects: Unwanted effects of a medicine alongside its intended action.
